name: Duerosuchus
sum: Duerosuchus is a basal crocodilian from the middle Eocene of Zamora, Spain, known from one incomplete skull.
wsnote: The skull is about 20 cm long; no reliable body-length estimate is given in the sources consulted.
holotype: A single incomplete but well preserved skull, with a lower jaw, some osteoderms and possibly some vertebrae, from Corrales del Vino, Zamora.
material: The holotype only, found by the amateur palaeontologists Luis Alonso Andrés and his son Luis Alonso Santiago.
biology: The species name piscator refers to a presumed ability to catch fish, inferred from the shape of its teeth.
author: Alonso Santiago and Alonso Andrés 2009

sources.text: L. Alonso Santiago and L. Alonso Andrés. 2009. Nuevo género de Crocodylia del Eoceno medio de la Península Ibérica (Zamora, España): Duerosuchus piscator nov. gen., nov. sp. Studia Geologica Salmanticensia 45(2):149-173
